blocks.content: While Article 323A contemplates establishment of tribunals only for public service matters by Parliament, Article 323B contemplates establishment of tribunals for other matters by both Parliament and State Legislatures.

rows: Other matters (Tax, Rent, Land Reforms, Foreign Exchange)
Hierarchy of tribunals can be created
Broad range of specified socio-economic topics

items: State Legislatures CANNOT establish administrative tribunals under Article 323A; this power is exclusively vested in Parliament.
Following the L. Chandra Kumar case (1997), decisions of tribunals are subject to judicial review before a Division Bench of the High Court first.
A hierarchy of tribunals can be created under Article 323B, but NO hierarchy can be created under Article 323A.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 323A deals exclusively with administrative tribunals for public service matters, whereas Article 323B covers tribunals for specified subjects like taxation, land reforms, and foreign exchange.
Tribunals under Article 323A can be created ONLY by Parliament, whereas tribunals under Article 323B can be created by both Parliament and State Legislatures within their competence.
Article 323A allows for no hierarchy of tribunals (only one tribunal for Union and one for each state/joint), whereas Article 323B permits a hierarchy of tribunals.
Both articles were inserted into the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
